messages:
laura: Quick sync — I'm rolling a small change to SDK auth precedence and sample apps. want to pick canonical env var names and rotation UX before I update docs.

matt: +1. what are you proposing?

laura: Proposal: single canonical API key env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. optional REDWOOD_ORG_ID and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID for client scoping. fallback order: 1) explicit args to client constructor, 2) env vars, 3) ~/.redwood/config (if present).

sophie: That seems sensible. can we keep old names supported for one release? lots of sample apps still use REDWOOD_KEY and RW_API_TOKEN.

laura: yes — plan is soft-deprecate: accept legacy names but log a one-time warning when present. remove after two releases.

dan: rotation: do we want SDK helpers for swapping keys at runtime? e.g., client.rotateKey(newKey) or encourage short-lived tokens with a refresh flow?

laura: Good Q. For most customers we'll keep long-lived API keys for simplicity. But SDK should provide: - a helper setApiKey(newKey) that updates in-memory credential for ongoing clients, and - a refresh hook interface so apps can plug in a token provider (async fn getToken()).

tia: for onboarding friction, sample apps should show both: 1) env var + simple start, 2) example with ephemeral refresh (curl -> exchange -> inject).

matt: can you paste an example snippet for env precedence and rotation?

laura: sure. we'll include this in README and quickstart.

laura: ```js
// precedence: constructor args > env vars > config file
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.CUSTOM_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
// runtime rotation helper
client.setApiKey = (k) => { client._auth.apiKey = k; /* internal swap, safe for current sessions */ };
// refresh hook style
const client = new RedwoodClient({ tokenProvider: async () => { return await fetch('/token').then(r=>r.text()); } });
```

sophie: love the tokenProvider pattern. for Python and Go we should mirror the same names and behavior. SDK parity note.

dan: need to clarify HTTP retry behavior: when rotation happens and you get 401 mid-request, SDK should attempt token refresh once then retry the request once. beyond that bubble error.

laura: agree. implement: on 401 -> if tokenProvider exists call it and retry once. add telemetry event auth.refresh_attempt.

deploy-bot: secret-scan: found long-lived key in playground-app .env -> flagged. expiring in 14d. :warning:

matt: ack. I'll rotate that key now. can we add guidance to the quickstart about not committing .env and enabling secret scan?

laura: yes. add a note and a sample .env.example with placeholders. also add CLI helper: `redwood keys rotate --name playground-app` that hits platform to create new key and prints ephemeral token example.

tia: docs action items?

laura: I'll open a small PR: 1) standardize env var names across README + samples, 2) add runtime setApiKey/tokenProvider examples, 3) document 401 refresh + retry semantics, 4) deprecation warning for legacy env names. target: one-week sprint.

sophie: please include a migration snippet for existing customers (REDWOOD_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY). small script people can run.

laura: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: sounds good. ping here when the PR is up so we can sweep sample apps.

laura: will do — thanks!
